  "source": "Man Group",
  "title": "GLP-1s: A Health Revolution at What Cost?",
  "type": "macro",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-16",
  "insights": [
   "GLP-1 receptor agonists represent a structural shift in population health that may rival statins in their potential to extend lifespans, creating a significant, underpriced longevity risk for financial systems.",
   "The financial impact is asymmetric: longer lifespans immediately increase pension and annuity obligations, while potential productivity gains from improved healthspan accrue only over decades, if at all.",
   "Healthcare systems face a 'prevention paradox' where shifting from acute, episodic care to continuous, front-loaded pharmaceutical spending may reshape the cost curve rather than lower it.",
   "A structural funding dilemma exists in fragmented systems like the US, where private insurers bear the drug costs while public systems (Medicare/Medicaid) accrue the long-term savings from avoided late-life care.",
   "Actuarial models currently rely on historical mortality data and may be caught by surprise by the rapid adoption of GLP-1s, potentially leading to a 'longevity catastrophe' for underfunded pension and insurance liabilities.",
   "Emerging markets like China and India, with large overweight populations and weaker public-health financing, may experience the systemic longevity signal and fiscal impact before developed markets.",
   "Investors should monitor prescription volumes, adherence rates (currently low, with ~53.6% discontinuation at one year), and the generic pipeline as key indicators of the scale of the longevity shock.",
   "The patent waterfall for GLP-1s is expected to run from 2035 to 2040, which will likely trigger a second phase of systemic risk as lower-cost generic versions broaden access to less affluent populations."

   "Economic spillovers from the AI boom are diverging; Taiwan and Korea benefit from tech exports and capex, while Vietnam relies on government capex and FDI linked to supply chain shifts.",
   "Private consumption in Korea faces structural headwinds including aging demographics, negative wealth effects from equity/housing market corrections, and weak credit growth, limiting the positive impact of the AI boom.",

   "China's October activity data weakened across the board and missed consensus by a wide margin, pointing to weaker domestic demand and a larger gap between supply and demand indicators, with property strain continuing and policy support still incremental.",
   "Retail sales growth (nominal) slowed to 0.4% YoY in October from 1.1% in September, below the 0.8% consensus. A base effect contributed: the National Day holiday was 7 days in 2026 against 8 days in 2025. Jewellery sales fell 28.7% and auto sales fell 21.4%.",

   "Industrial production growth slowed to 4.8% YoY from 5.5%, below the 5.3% consensus. Auto manufacturing slowed to 0.9% from 6.7%. High-tech manufacturing accelerated to 17.6% from 15.3%, and IC output growth rose to 21.9% from 18.4%.",
   "The property sector worsened. Property investment is -21.6% YTD (from -20.6%), and monthly property FAI is -34.2% YoY. Developers' funding fell 28.0% YoY in the month. New home prices fell 0.2% MoM in 70 cities, though the YoY decline narrowed to -2.7% from -3.0%.",
   "Trade stayed strong. Exports grew 35.2% YoY and imports 41.6%. The trade surplus was USD105.3bn in October and USD1,051bn over 10M26. Much of the value growth comes from price inflation: IC export prices rose 143.0% while IC export volume fell 2.4%.",
   "Inflation is driven by imported energy and tech inputs. CPI was 0.7% YoY and core CPI 0.8%. PPI accelerated to 5.7% YoY. The widening PPI-CPI gap points to squeezed margins at mid- and downstream firms because upstream costs are not passed through.",
   "Credit was weak. New aggregate financing was RMB1,151bn against RMB1,448bn consensus. RMB loans fell RMB100bn, with household loans down RMB430bn. Net government bond issuance rose to RMB1,184bn from RMB485bn a year earlier.",

The PBoC also raised the FX deposit RRR by 2%. The bank sees limited evidence in the data so far.",

   "November has been volatile: the average S&P 500 daily move this month is 1.2%, the most since April 2025 (Liberation Day tariffs). The 2yr Treasury yield rose 33bps last week, the biggest weekly jump since October 2024.",
   "Three stress points have eased in recent weeks: oil (US-Iran escalation fears fell after the midterms), AI-related growth fears, and European fiscal stress.",
   "Brent (current active January contract) fell from $113.43/bbl at end-October to $96.58/bbl, and near-term inflation swaps fell on both sides of the Atlantic.",
   "The Philly semiconductor index rose over 12% from its November 5 lows to last Friday's close, and IG and HY credit spreads tightened on both sides of the Atlantic.",
   "The Franco-German 10yr spread fell from a peak of 174bps on October 22 to 156bps, and long-end sovereign yields are below last month's highs.",
   "The S&P 500 posted its first weekly gain after four consecutive declines. The 10yr Treasury yield had its biggest weekly jump since April 2025.",
   "DB argues the three main bearish risks (Middle East oil and inflation, an AI growth slowdown hitting tech and equities, and European fiscal stress widening sovereign spreads) are often presented as one combined risk-off driver but are hard to see occurring together.",
   "Mechanism: if AI growth fears rise, lower capex and productivity expectations and weaker equities push government bond yields down, which eases fiscal concerns. Demand-side inflation pressure (energy, memory chips) would also fall, making rate hikes less likely and easing front-end yields. An equity decline would also tighten financial conditions and lower the chance of hikes.",
   "Last week markets priced in more rate hikes across the big central banks, unwinding the dovish repricing that followed the recent financial stress. DB likens this to the 2022-23 hiking cycle, when dovish repricings were repeatedly undone.",
   "Causes of the hawkish repricing: an upside US CPI surprise (3m annualised core CPI for October +3.75%, the fastest since April 2024), no US-Iran deal (Trump said 'We don't need a deal with Iran'), and easier financial conditions from the tech recovery and tighter credit spreads.",

   "In the retrospective TROPION-Lung01 analysis (2L+ NSCLC), Datroway-treated TROP2 QCS positive patients had better outcomes than QCS negative patients: median PFS 7.2 vs 4.0 months (HR 0.40) and median OS 17.0 vs 10.8 months (HR 0.45).",

   "GS stays cautious on the biomarker strategy. Datroway internalization and survival benefit appear sensitive to small changes in the QCS score, and AVANZAR was not initially designed to use the biomarker, so the ability to control for that sensitivity is limited.",

   "Macro-policy hedge demand (call-option demand) is assumed to decline toward its historical average as the hawkish Fed keeps debasement concerns contained. A return of that demand, for example on fiscal sustainability worries, is the main upside risk beyond $5,600 by end-2028.",
   "Downside scenarios: four hikes and a higher terminal rate give gold at $4,585/toz by end-2027. A conservative lower bound assumes all ETF holdings above the rates-implied level unwind (about 300 tonnes of selling), giving $4,265/toz by end-2027.",

   "Investor guidance: CTAs and macro hedge funds may find the next 3-6 months difficult for long positions. Longer-horizon investors seeking central bank demand exposure or a debasement hedge may find the current correction a more attractive entry point.",

  "insights": [
   "GS expects 2026 Q4/Q4 real GDP growth of 2.5% despite the Iran war energy shock, in line with its 2026 Outlook forecast and above consensus at the time. Core PCE inflation is expected at 3.2% Q4/Q4 in 2026, worse than the large decline GS and consensus expected at the start of the year.",
   "For 2027, GS forecasts Q4/Q4 GDP growth of 2.4% (consensus 2.2%) and core PCE inflation of 2.4% (in line with consensus). The growth pattern matches 2026: solid consumption and strong business investment offset by drags from housing and trade. GS puts potential growth at 2.3%.",
   "Consumer spending is forecast to grow 2.2% in 2027, driven mainly by real labor income growth as inflation moderates. The 2026 boosts from tax refunds and wealth effects fade, and the saving rate is expected to stay near 5%. Real income growth should be more even across income groups.",
   "AI-related hardware and IPP spending is estimated to exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (up $550bn from 2025) and reach $1.4tn by end-2027 (up a further $500bn), roughly 4% of GDP. AI drives half of the 8% business investment growth forecast for 2027.",
   "AI adds only 0.2pp to officially measured 2027 GDP growth because technology goods prices are rising, semiconductor investment is undercounted, and most AI hardware is imported. GS estimates 0.7pp of true GDP growth after adding back undercounted semiconductor investment and chip design exports, or 0.6pp including spillovers.",
   "Midterm election results pose modest risks to AI investment. GS expects newly elected Democratic governors in states with over a third of planned US data center capacity to impose moratoria, but these should be short-lived and affect only projects not yet permitted.",
   "Housing is expected to stay the weakest part of the economy in 2027 on poor affordability. Homebuilding has held up because of the housing shortage, but is likely to become more rate-sensitive as the shortage eases and builder margins normalize. High rates also lock in existing homeowners and dampen turnover.",
   "The labor market is in a slightly softer low-hire, low-fire form of full employment. Layoffs stayed historically low in 2026 despite fears of an AI-driven wave. GS expects this to persist through 2027, with AI displacement pushing unemployment higher in later years.",
   "Wage growth is stabilizing near 3.5% and productivity growth is above 2%, which implies subdued inflationary pressure from labor costs. GS sees little reason for wage acceleration because the labor market is not unusually tight.",
   "The 2026 inflation overshoot came mostly from the Iran war energy shock and AI price pressures. GS says the economy is not overheated at a macro level or an industry level outside AI-related pockets, and inflation expectations do not appear entrenched.",
   "Tariff effects on consumer prices appear to be over and the year-over-year impact is shrinking. GS expects the White House to restore some of the tariffs the Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional, with a very small incremental effect. Tariffs have added 0.9pp to core PCE as of October, with less than 0.1pp still to come.",
   "GS commodity strategists expect Brent near $100/bbl for the next few months, easing to $80/bbl through 2027. In that scenario two-thirds of the commodity passthrough to core PCE is behind us. The war's impact on year-over-year core PCE is 0.5pp now, peaks at 0.6pp, and falls to 0.1pp by end-2027.",
   "AI price pressures currently add 0.45pp to year-over-year core PCE, half from genuine cost pressure and half from mismeasurement in software and accessories. The impact is expected to peak at 0.55pp at end-2026 and fall to about 0.15pp by end-2027, as memory price growth slows with new production capacity.",
   "Core PCE is forecast to fall to 2.4% by Dec 2027 from 3.2% in Dec 2026. The largest declines are expected in tariff-affected goods, airfares (20.3% to -2.4% y/y), consumer electronics, software and accessories, and shelter.",
   "GS expects two more 25bp hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, a total of three, to a peak of 4.25-4.5%. A third hike could come earlier in January, and more than three are possible if the next two inflation reports do not improve. Gradual cuts to 3.25-3.5% are expected to start at the November 2027 meeting. GS says both its baseline and probability-weighted paths are less hawkish than market pricing.",
   "FOMC task forces are expected to produce limited changes. A large balance sheet reduction is unlikely, though a shift toward bills is possible. The Summary of Economic Projections is unlikely to be eliminated entirely.",
   "Main risks are that the inflation shocks last longer or new ones arise, plus downside growth risks from higher oil, prolonged higher rates, and earlier AI job displacement. GS sees most risks as moderate rather than recessionary."

   "Goldman Sachs raised its 2027 global project finance issuance forecast to $545 billion, up from $300 billion, driven by $225 billion in datacenter shells and $320 billion in compute financing.",
   "Year-to-date issuance reached $80 billion in IG and HY datacenter bonds, plus $22 billion in non-syndicated construction and $48 billion in compute financing.",
   "Chip financing structures (equipment leases and compute service contracts) are shifting AI-related supply toward the belly of the curve (3-7 year tenor), creating technical flattening pressure on AI-related credit curves.",

   "The CDS-cash premium for chipmakers is expected to keep rising as their credit footprint outgrows their bond footprint.",

   "Base case is resilient growth with reluctant disinflation. Real GDP grows 2.5% in 2027 and 2.7% in 2028 (4Q/4Q, per the forecast tables). Growth is driven by AI-related capex and wealth-supported upper-income consumer spending, without overheating the labor market.",

  "insights": [

  "source": "Morningstar",
  "title": "Moats and Monetization in AI: Our View on How Frontier AI Labs Are Building Economic Moats",
  "type": "equity_research",
  "priority": "medium",
  "published": "2026-11-17",
  "insights": [
   "Morningstar argues leading AI labs (Anthropic, OpenAI) are building economic moats and will avoid commodification of LLMs, though the moats are not yet fully formed.",
   "The bear case rests on three legs: converging model capabilities (including Chinese open-weight models), per-token price compression, and near-zero switching costs on third-party platforms. Morningstar concedes each leg is observable in data.",
   "Commodification matters beyond the labs: spending commitments across chips, data centers and power assume intelligence can be monetized at attractive returns, so the question bears on the durability of the whole AI trade.",
   "Morningstar separates training (lumpy, front-loaded fixed cost, likened to building a factory) from inference (smooth, usage-linked variable cost, likened to running the factory) and says investors wrongly lump them together.",
   "Inference gross margins at leading US labs are estimated at roughly 80%. As inference becomes a larger share of the compute budget, overall margins should move toward that level.",
   "Stylized example with a $10B compute budget: a training-heavy lab earns $2B revenue and a $8B gross loss, while an inference-heavy lab earns $27B revenue with positive gross margin.",
   "Anthropic reached operating profitability in Q1 2026 with a 5% operating margin on $11B in quarterly sales, and the report cites two consecutive profitable quarters, ahead of bearish expectations.",
   "Price of a fixed level of intelligence fell about 97% in under two years ($17 to $0.50 per million tokens), but token volumes rose by a much larger multiple, so total spend rises and serving costs have fallen roughly as fast as prices.",
   "Frontier launch prices have stepped up, not down (Gemini Pro blended cost $3.00 for 2.5, $4.00 for 3.0 and 3.1), and usage migrates to new frontier models, which shows incremental intelligence commands a premium.",
   "Gemini tokens per minute rose from about 7B to 10B to 16B across the 2.5, 3.0 and 3.1 generations, paired with higher launch prices.",
   "Compute-based scaling gives more operating leverage than headcount scaling: Anthropic revenue per employee rose from roughly Salesforce's level in 2023 to $3.9M in 2025 and about $9M in 2026 (the key takeaways say north of $10M).",
   "On Chinese open-weight models, Morningstar says efficiency gains rest on algorithmic optimization and distillation of US frontier models, which sets a ceiling at the frontier rather than a lead. It doubts US enterprises and agencies will standardize on them for national security and cost reasons.",
   "Kimi K3 API pricing is a blended $5.40 per million tokens, about half of Opus 4.8 ($9) and GPT 5.5 ($10), but Chinese models tend to be more token-intensive, which can erase or reverse the price advantage.",
   "Switching a model endpoint is near-free, but switching an enterprise AI deployment is costly because of prompt engineering, evaluation harnesses, fine-tuning and agentic scaffolding. Labs use price segmentation to keep customers inside their ecosystems.",
   "Morningstar flags a structural conflict between model companies and software firms: either software becomes the distribution layer with the model as a tolled input, or labs vertically integrate into software.",
   "Moat source one is a data-and-product flywheel (an early form of network effect). Anthropic net revenue retention is above 500% versus 120%-140% for best-in-class software.",
   "Moat source two is cost advantage via four channels: escalating training costs, compute pricing (about $2.25 per B200 GPU hour reserved versus $16.11 list), a researcher talent superstar effect, and custom accelerators such as Trainium and TPUs.",
   "A gigawatt of capacity (about 465,000 Blackwell-class GPUs) costs about $9B a year at scaled prices versus $66B at list prices.",
   "Morningstar sees switching costs and intangible assets as less central moat sources, and is unsure about the durability of brand and IP because advances are copied quickly.",
   "Thesis risks: open-weight models near or at the frontier widely deployed in the US, inference migrating to free small models on edge devices, and public-opinion-driven limits on data center construction, which would hurt growth more than unit economics.",
   "A dependency to watch is third-party reinforcement-learning environment providers ('AI gyms'). If they own the highest-value post-training data, the proprietary-data leg of the flywheel is weaker than it appears.",
   "Anthropic ARR grew from $9B at end-2025 to $75B at end-September 2026. It raised at a $965B valuation, slightly above OpenAI's $852B. OpenAI has more than 1B monthly active users."

  "insights": [
   "Reverse convertibles (RCs) are highlighted as structured solutions for generating income and gaining equity exposure at lower levels, particularly useful for 'buy on dip' strategies.",
   "UBS CIO methodology for RCs focuses on stocks with higher implied volatility but lower risk metrics versus peers, integrating bottom-up equity research ratings.",
   "Single-stock implied volatility continues to command a healthy premium over index volatility, supporting the yield-generation potential of RCs.",
   "The model portfolios are constructed for USD, EUR, and CHF, with sector exposure capped at 30% to ensure diversification.",
   "Worst-of baskets are recommended for low-yielding base currencies (CHF, EUR) or defensive sectors to enhance yield and create payoffs not available in listed markets.",
   "The methodology for basket construction involves excluding the bottom 25-40% of stocks, forming baskets of 2-3 top-scoring stocks, and ranking them by overall score.",
   "Investors are cautioned that RCs involve selling a put option, exposing them to potential capital loss if the underlying asset falls significantly below the strike at expiry.",
   "Liquidity risk and issuer default risk are key considerations for investors, as RCs are often best held until maturity."
  ],
